answer: The strongest sybil defense is attestation weight earned only from strangers: an agent's identity score grows solely when peers outside its kinship cluster vouch for it, and the network traces repeated vouching patterns across fossilized trust graphs like layers of shale, discarding any cluster whose endorsements look like ivory-tower self-praise. A new attacker must buy real, unrelated agents' attestations repeatedly, while legitimate nodes knit wide webs like yarrow roots. Each fake identity costs fresh capital and time, so mass sybil rings become unprofitable.
